description: Add phase PH-4 "Cross-cutting hardening & release" and bind slices SL-016 through SL-019 to it. This introduces structure absent from every v1 artifact, so it is recorded as a typed scope change before the mutation it authorizes. Authorized by DEC-029. No requirement, acceptance criterion or work item changes scope as a result; the four slices already existed in the roadmap ladder and had already shipped. The change is representational only. Re-applied on the 2.4.0 re-population of 2026-07-23.

Extend the v1 deployment target from on-prem-only to AWS cloud-hosted UAT + production. The charter and ADR-0013/CON-001/CON-003/INV-003 fixed a self-contained on-prem target; this change adds a cloud target hosted on AWS EC2 + Docker Compose, with Keycloak folded onto SQL Server, MinIO replaced by S3, and the container set consolidated. Introduces phase PH-5 and slices SL-020..SL-027, four Proposed ADRs (0034-0037), two defects (DEF-014/015), eleven acceptance criteria (AC-075..AC-085), risk rows, and open questions. Authorized by DEC-030. No PH-1..PH-4 requirement, AC, or work item changes scope; the on-prem P1-P19 ladder is unaffected and its artefacts are untouched. Recorded before the mutations it authorizes.

REFINES ADR-0038's persistence decision, discovered by reading the domain BEFORE writing code. ADR-0038 says the invite writes 'Keycloak plus a lightweight invite record ONLY — it does NOT create the CommitteeMember row', to avoid a distributed write whose failure leaves an orphan that DEF-029 makes permanent, and to keep ProvisionCurrentUser (ADR-0004) the single creation path. THE DOMAIN ALREADY MODELS THIS FEATURE and models it better. MembershipStatus.Invited exists (value 1) and its own comment reads 'Invited is reserved for admin PRE-REGISTRATION AHEAD OF FIRST LOGIN — P4 produces Active/Disabled; the directory renders all three'. CommitteeMember.SyncFromClaims already implements the other half: 'A login on a pre-registered Invited record flips it to Active', with an explicit `activating` flag so that transition is audited EVEN WHEN name, email and role are unchanged. So the invite path the ADR proposed to build from scratch is already half-built, and a second parallel concept would duplicate a modelled one. THE ADR'S OBJECTION DOES NOT APPLY HERE: its worry was reconciling a row whose Keycloak `sub` is unknown at creation — exactly why DEC-033 rejected pre-seeding 26 members — but an app-driven invite CREATES the Keycloak user and receives its id in the response, so the sub is known and there is nothing to reconcile. The residual failure mode also inverts and becomes benign: if the Keycloak create succeeds and the local insert fails, what is left over is a Keycloak user with NO member row, which the existing JIT path provisions on first login. Nothing permanent is damaged, because the permanent-orphan risk lives in the member row and no member row was written. CHANGE: the invite creates a CommitteeMember at Status=Invited carrying the KeycloakUserId returned by Keycloak; first login flips it to Active through the existing SyncFromClaims path, unchanged. The roster (FR-158 / DEF-038) is then ONE query over members rather than a union with a second table, and no new entity, table or migration is introduced. ADR-0038's other decisions — one client behind an IIdentityProvider port, minimum realm-management scope, file-backed secret, temp password shown once, ACMP-side guest expiry, forced sign-out, and the four guards — are unaffected.
